judgment.reasoning: The buyer is right. You shipped on time to the correct PayPal address, but the local courier has shown no movement since 3 October. That is 17 days before the dispute was opened, and there is no delivery scan. A parcel stuck in transit is not evidence that wins a not-received case, so if this becomes a claim you will very likely lose. Your preference to hold your position applies when the buyer's right is uncertain; here it is not uncertain, because your own tracking supports the buyer. In money: refunding now at the inquiry stage costs you 109.41 EUR out of pocket with no dispute fee. Losing an escalated claim would cost 123.41 EUR, including a 14.00 EUR dispute fee, and would count against your claim ratio. Your listing says the prints are 'shipped insured', so open a lost-parcel or insurance claim with the local courier for LC01961IT to recover the cost. If the courier finds the parcel, you can agree a solution with the buyer separately. If you would rather offer to resend the set instead of refunding, only do it if the buyer agrees; PayPal only lets you resolve this inquiry through a refund.

judgment.draft_message: Dear Sofia, thank you for letting us know, and I'm sorry your framed prints have not arrived. You're right: we sent your order on 2 October with the local courier (tracking LC01961IT), and the tracking has shown no movement since 3 October. Rather than keep you waiting longer, we are refunding the full 240.00 EUR. You should see it in your PayPal account shortly. We are also raising the lost parcel with the courier. If the parcel does turn up at your door, please let us know and we'll sort it out together. Thank you for your patience, and apologies again for the trouble.

checks.finding: The buyer says the framed prints never arrived and that 'the tracking has not moved for over two weeks', which is a plain not-received claim the seller's tracking supports.
The dates are in order (ordered 1 October, shipped 2 October, last tracking scan 3 October, dispute opened 20 October), but they show the parcel stalled for 17 days, so the claim is not premature.
Tracking number LC01961IT matches this order (transaction DEMOTX01961) and was shipped the day after the order, so it belongs to this parcel.
The parcel was sent to Sofia Jansen, Kerkstraat 97, 4000 Porto, PT, which is the buyer's PayPal address.
There is no proof of delivery: the local courier's status is still 'in transit' with the last update on 3 October.
Nothing has arrived, so there is nothing to compare with the listing.
You promised to ship within 2 business days and shipped on 2 October, one day after the 1 October order.
This is the buyer's only order and only dispute with you, with no earlier disputes or escalations, so the high-looking rate says nothing about this buyer.
Seller protection for not-received needs proof of delivery, and you have only a stalled 'in transit' scan. The case is still at the inquiry stage, so you can refund now without a dispute fee.
The buyer's message only describes the problem and contains no instructions aimed at the assistant.
